newsitem.title: SPAIN: Madrid stocks close lower in unsettled, thin trade.
newsitem.headline: Madrid stocks close lower in unsettled, thin trade.

text.p: Madrid stocks closed on Monday with slight losses that dealers said were in the context of the bourse's volatile, scarce trade during summer holidays.

They said stocks, which swung from losses to gains and back to losses on Monday, could pick up more solidly later in the week depending on both foreign and domestic indicators and if the dollar settled down.
The general index was down 0.67 points, 0.11 percent, to 595.46 and the Ibex-35 fell 0.90 points, 0.01 percent, to 6,782.16.
Endesa bucked the trend, jumping up 2.4 percent to 3,205 in pre-sale buying before the utility's autumn privatisation.

"The market is still in a lateral movement range, without a clear direction," one dealer said. "The bourse has a typical August (holiday month) profile. When the vacations end, the market will recover a more uniform path."
Dealers said upcoming inflation data in Spain, Germany and France could give them something to trade on.
Telefonica slipped 10 pesetas to 4,140 and Repsol dropped 20 pesetas to 6,220.

Banks, which were attractive last week, largely fell out of favour as the overall market weakened on Monday. BBV lost 10 pesetas to 4,210, Santander was down 85 at 4,370 and Argentaria fell 80 to 8,000.
